doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Jerry Jerome sends him to the Harry James rehearsal
summary: Meeting Jerry Jerome at the subway, he went to Nola Studios and asked Harry James for a job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you had decided by this time that I’m a musician and this is what I’m doing for the rest of my life?
Oh yeah, no, I was being a professional, I thought I was a professional, and then I saw Jerry Jerome, I don’t know if you recall that name.

Tenor saxophone player. I was going into the subway of Jackson Heights, to go into town, and he was coming out of it. And he says, “Hey Jackson, where you going?” I says, “I’m going in town” you know, “and see what’s happening at the Nola studios.” He says, “Harry James is starting — you know Harry from Benny Goodman’s band?” I says, “Well I don’t know him personally.” He says, “He’s rehearsing his first band.” He says, “Go to the Nola Studios and tell them I suggested you talk to him.” See and I did. I went there and to make a long story short, I waited until they took a break and I went up to Harry and I says, “Jerry Jerome suggested I talk to you, Harry.” He says, “I know you, Jack Palmer from Red Norvo’s band.” He says, “I saw you at the Famous Door.” I says, “Yeah.” He says, “You don’t want to join my band” he says, “you’ll never get a chance to play,” he says you know, and he says, “because I know you like to play jazz.” I says, “I don’t care.” I says, “I like to hear you” and I says, “so I don’t mind not playing. I’d love to be with the band.” And it was an excellent band.
